profile.summary: ProteinZero V2 designs amino acid sequences for a protein backbone that you supply. It starts from ProteinMPNN and improves it with online reinforcement learning: the model generates sequences, those sequences are folded by ESMFold and scored for structural agreement and predicted stability, and the reward is used to update the model. Two teaser checkpoints are released, for structures of up to about 100 residues.

summary_quotes.text: ProteinZero V2 teaser checkpoints for structure-conditioned protein sequence design. The checkpoints use ProteinMPNN as the base model.
Reward signals combine structural feedback from ESMFold with the fast ΔΔG score introduced in ProteinZero V1.
ProteinZero is an online reinforcement learning framework that enables protein generative models to continuously improve by learning from their own outputs.
These checkpoints are intended for structures of up to 100 residues.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The base model is ProteinMPNN, loaded with 128-dimensional node and edge features, three encoder and three decoder layers and 48 neighbours per residue. Reinforcement learning then trains it against rewards rather than a single supervised target: the V2 README names structural feedback from ESMFold and the fast change in folding free energy introduced in V1. V1 used GRPO; the V2 checkpoints were trained with PARPO, an algorithm the authors describe as aimed at exploring Pareto frontiers in multi-objective optimisation, and whose formulation is not yet published.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two V2 checkpoints are released, differing only in which structure predictor gave the reward: proteinzero_v2_esmfold1.pt (ESMFold1) and proteinzero_v2_esmfold2.pt (ESMFold2). A result must name which of the two was used, the sampling temperature and the seed, since generation samples. They are described as teaser checkpoints, with full checkpoints and a paper to follow, so results may not be reproducible against later releases. The earlier ProteinZero V1 is a different model, built on InstructPLM.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Inverse folding model: it designs an amino acid sequence for a given protein backbone. ProteinZero V2 is a ProteinMPNN model further trained by online reinforcement learning.

quotes.text: ProteinZero V2 teaser checkpoints for structure-conditioned protein sequence design. The checkpoints use ProteinMPNN as the base model.
ProteinZero is an online reinforcement learning framework that enables protein generative models to continuously improve by learning from their own outputs.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: ProteinMPNN. The V2 README gives the constructor arguments to load the checkpoints: ca_only=False, num_letters=21, node_features=128, edge_features=128, hidden_dim=128, num_encoder_layers=3, num_decoder_layers=3, augment_eps=0.0, dropout=0.0, k_neighbors=48. The released files are plain ProteinMPNN state dictionaries.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A directory of backbone PDB files, read non-recursively in filename order, with a sampling temperature and a number of sequences per backbone.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: A tab-separated file with the columns structure_id, sample_id and sequence; one row per generated sequence. Chains of a multichain structure are separated by a slash. Nothing is folded or scored.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: Not reported. The V2 README gives the ProteinMPNN constructor arguments (hidden_dim 128, three encoder and three decoder layers, k_neighbors 48) but no parameter count, and the counts in INSTALL.md belong to the V1 InstructPLM pipeline.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: Not reported for the V2 checkpoints. The repository's training documentation describes the V1 pipeline, which trains an InstructPLM-based model on the released CATH 4.3 chain-level dataset; the V2 README does not say what its checkpoints were trained on.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: Two teaser checkpoints in the repository: ProteinZero-V2/checkpoints/proteinzero_v2_esmfold1.pt (structural feedback from ESMFold1) and proteinzero_v2_esmfold2.pt (ESMFold2). The README says full checkpoints will follow. ProteinZero V1, built on InstructPLM, is the published version.

A CPU is enough; the device argument accepts cpu, cuda or auto.

notes: The existing HyInv source (hyinv-20261106-source-report) cites ProteinZero only as arXiv 2506.07459 in its reference list; the repository URL came from that arXiv abstract page, which names it. The HyInv report PDF cannot be quoted by the checker and was not kept as a saved source. The report evaluates two variants it calls ProteinZero V2 (ESM1) and ProteinZero V2 (ESM2); these look like the two released checkpoints, which differ in the ESMFold version used for the reward, but the mapping is inferred and stated by neither side. ProteinZero V1 (arXiv 2506.07459, TMLR) is a separate model built on InstructPLM and may be a separate record. No V2 paper exists yet.
